reason: The nucleus contains opened DNA and nearby enzymes, while nucleotides supply the building blocks for copying it.
expectation: The cell will replicate its DNA in preparation for division.

effect: The genome is copied, but sister chromatids still need to be separated before division.
reaction: The distinction between copying the genome and making proteins is useful.
reason: Centrosomes organize spindle microtubules, and tubulin and motor proteins provide the spindle's components.
expectation: These components will form a spindle for separating the copied chromosomes.

effect: The spindle is assembled, but the copied chromosomes have not yet been separated.
reaction: The picture makes clear that spindle assembly is not separation itself.
reason: The spindle should act on the copied genome to separate its sister chromatids.
expectation: The spindle will help separate the copied chromosomes toward opposite sides of the cell.

effect: The chromosome sets are separated, but the cell still needs to divide its shared cytoplasm.
reaction: The distinction between chromosome separation and cell division is clear.
reason: The cell needs more membrane as it grows and prepares to form two cells; phospholipids supply its membrane material.
expectation: The phospholipids will contribute to growth of the cell's membrane.

effect: Phospholipids and new proteins formed membrane vesicles; they have not yet been added to the cell surface.
reaction: I expected direct membrane growth, so the vesicle intermediate was a surprise.
reason: The new vesicles appear to provide membrane material for the growing cell.
expectation: The vesicles will add membrane to the cell as it prepares to divide.

effect: The vesicles contributed to an enlarged cell body with more cytoplasm and membrane; the separated chromosome sets still need to be brought together with the division machinery.
reaction: The growth result clarified why the vesicle intermediate mattered.
reason: Actin and myosin beneath the membrane can form the contractile machinery that divides the enlarged cell.
expectation: The cell will develop a contractile furrow or other machinery for dividing its cytoplasm.

effect: The actin and myosin have no available operation yet, so another preparation may be needed before cytokinesis.
reaction: The failed attempt leaves the timing of the contractile machinery unclear.
reason: The enlarged cell body and separated chromosome sets represent complementary parts of the same cell that need to be brought together.

choice.with: Separated chromosome sets inside the cell

expectation: This will integrate the separated chromosome sets into the enlarged cell, potentially enabling division.
